description.value: The study investigated differences in regional gray matter volume between chronic cigarette smokers and matched non-smoking controls using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry.

spans.text: To further investigate the effects of chronic cigarette smoking on structural brain changes, we applied whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to quantify regional gray matter volume between 44 otherwise healthy chronic cigarette smokers and 44 matched non-smoking control subjects.

design.value: A cross-sectional whole-brain voxel-based morphometry study comparing 44 chronic cigarette smokers with 44 matched non-smoking control subjects.

spans.text: MRI study was carried for 44 smokers and 44 matched non-smokers to assess gray matter volume differences between the two groups.
To examine differences in regional gray matter volume between groups, a voxel-wise two-sample t-test analysis in SPM5 and total gray matter volume was set as covariates.
In the VBM analysis, gray matter volume was lower in the smokers that in the non-smokers group in the left thalamus, left medial frontal cortex (Brodmann area 10) and left anterior cingulated

To further investigate the effects of chronic cigarette smoking on structural brain changes, we applied whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to quantify regional gray matter volume between 44 otherwise healthy chronic cigarette smokers and 44 matched non-smoking control subjects.

In the VBM analysis, gray matter volume was lower in the smokers that in the non-smokers group in the left thalamus, left medial frontal cortex (Brodmann area 10) and left anterior cingulated (see Fig. 1 and Table 1).
